name: MD-08
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Jamie Raskin running with $7.9M on hand
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~97%
model.rationale: Raskin is a well-funded incumbent in a D+30 district, while Cheryl Riley has raised under $17,000, leaving no plausible path to a competitive race. Markets and fundamentals both point to a lopsided Democratic win.
model.watch: Only a major unforeseen scandal or incumbent retirement scenario could meaningfully narrow this margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Maryland's 8th District is one of the most Democratic-leaning seats in the country, with a partisan lean of D+30. Jamie Raskin, a prominent incumbent, is seeking another term and holds a massive financial advantage, with nearly $7.9 million in cash on hand. Republican challenger Cheryl Riley has raised about $16,600, and a Green Party candidate is also on the ballot with minimal resources.

No public polling or expert ratings exist for this race, but prediction markets put the Democratic win probability around 97%. The fundamentals, incumbency, and fundraising gap all point to a comfortable Raskin victory, with the only real question being the size of the margin.
